# Consumer build tooling drifts from the root lockfile

## Context

The installed-consumer check stops before compiling runtime code. On Engine PR #20365 at `50ef8a2cbe`, [Consumer Runtime Build job 127467932737](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/42090786010/job/127467932737) fails during its second fixture install:

```
npm install --include=dev --no-audit --no-fund --ignore-scripts
ETARGET No matching version found for playwright-core@1.65.0
```

At 19:31Z on November 5, a fresh npm query still returned E404 for that exact version. The published `playwright@1.65.0` requires it. Grace and Vega independently observed the same partial publication.

## The Problem

The fixture copies the installed package's development dependency ranges and resolves them afresh. Its `@playwright/test ^1.63.0` selects 1.65.0, while the root lockfile resolves 1.64.1. Runtime build evidence therefore depends on an unrelated upstream development-tool release completing. Retrying before the missing package appears cannot reach the builds.

## The Architectural Reality

`buildScripts/util/check-consumer-runtime-build.mjs#main` owns pack → physical consumer install → hoisted build-tool install → browser generation → Data/Canvas/App/Main compilation. `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/checkConsumerRuntimeBuild.spec.mjs` owns its cheap rule tests. The workflow only invokes this guard.

Design authority: its module summary says it builds runtime entries “from an installed copy of this package, because this repository's own build structurally cannot observe what a consumer's build does.” Its purpose is consumer resolution, not testing the newest development-tool publication. The last surface contributor confirmed no active claim or fresh-semver requirement.

## The Fix

Resolve each declared fixture development dependency to its exact top-level version in the checked-in root `package-lock.json`. Preserve the declared package set and overrides, install them at the consumer root, and retain every physical layout and runtime assertion. Reject absent or stale lockfile resolutions with the package named; never substitute this seat's installed `node_modules`.

This pins direct build-tool versions only. It does not promise a fully frozen transitive dependency tree or change runtime dependency ranges.

| Surface | Source of authority | Behavior | Failure | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Consumer guard's build-tool install | Existing guard summary and root lockfile | Exact locked direct dev versions, hoisted in the physical fixture | Missing/mismatched resolution fails explicitly | Owning helper JSDoc | Focused controls + full physical guard |
| Consumer runtime checks | Existing worker/addon/artifact expectations | All current checks retained | Same nonzero failure behavior | Existing module contract | Full physical guard |

Decision Record impact: none; localized build-instrument repair, no runtime architecture change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The fixture's declared direct development-tool versions come from root lock resolutions, including `@playwright/test`, rather than fresh semver selection or local installed versions.
- [ ] Missing, unusable or manifest-mismatched lock entries fail explicitly; focused tests distinguish these from a valid lock and prove input preservation.
- [ ] The real guard still packs source, installs a separate consumer under an `apps/` ancestor, hoists its toolchain, generates browser assets and runs every existing runtime build/assertion.
- [ ] No CI check is disabled and no dependency range, release or package policy is changed.

## Out of Scope

Full transitive fixture lock synthesis, dependency upgrades, source-only package-policy changes, CI tier selection, and the theme generator in #3589.

## Avoided Traps

No passing off a fresh-registry ETARGET as a runtime build failure; no mocked consumer layout, copied producer artifacts, nested toolchain, `node_modules` version fallback or skipped build arms. Waiting for upstream would clear this incident but retain the same exposure to the next unrelated direct-tool release.

Related: #19470, #17868, #20365.
